reporting-org.narrative:
RLP is an outreach project for the School of Law, Makerere University, established in 1999 in response to research that indicated that refugees and asylum seekers do not fully enjoy their rights in Uganda. Its initial focus on the provision of Legal Aid and Psychosocial support to displaced people has since expanded and is now organised under five thematic programme areas;  Access to Justice  Conflict, Transitional Justice and Governance  Gender & Sexuality  Media for Social Change  Mental Health & Psychosocial Wellbeing
Currently, RLP has ten (10) offices across the country with 167 employees with a gender disaggregation of 97Males and 70 Females from diverse backgrounds of professional disciplines, cultures and expertise, and with 32% of staff being refugees.
RLP’s primary goal is to provide legal aid to refugees, asylum seekers, internally displaced persons and deportees. Over the years, RLP has grown into a ‘Leading Centre for Justice and Forced Migrants’, conducting cutting-edge research, evidence-based advocacy, and providing pro-bono legal aid services to forced migrants in various gazette refugee settlements refugee-hosting districts across Uganda.
Vision RLP envisions a context where all people enjoy their human rights, irrespective of legal status. This vision is informed by relevant international laws and the Constitution of the Republic of Uganda.
Mission RLP’s mission is to empower asylum seekers, refugees, deportees, IDPs and host communities to enjoy their human rights and lead dignified lives.
Mandate RLP strikes to; 1. Promote the protection, well-being and dignity of displaced people and their hosts 2. Empower forced migrants, communities and all associated actors to challenge and combat injustices in policy, law and practice 3. Influence national and international debate on matters of forced migration, justice and peace 4. Be a resource for forced migrants and relevant actors.
Core Values RLP’s core values are; i. Independence ii. Innovation iii. Non-discrimination iv. Respect v. Professionalism vi. Accountability vii. Rigour

budget-line.narrative: To Enhance Mental Health and Livelihood for Refugees and hosts to reduce dependency on relief, broaden and diversify household incomes, and reduce poverty and its associated vices to enable refugees and hosts to contribute to national development
To improve access and uptake of professional and timely service for profound war-related, gendered and sexual reproductive health and rights (SRHR) harms experienced by refugees and host communities
To improve the capacity of Rule of Law Stakeholders to effectively interact with complex refugee communities and hosts
To influence refugee-related policies by regional and international stakeholders
To promote peaceful co-existence in and around refugee hosting areas

recipient-country.narrative: Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands who are the funders of this project
